flashcards.back: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, pictured as an arrow: the arrow for (2, 3) moves 2 right and 3 up.
The length of the vector arrow: for (x, y) it is sqrt(x^2 + y^2) by Pythagoras, so |(2, 3)| = sqrt(13).
The record of a vector as its components stacked in a column: the top entry is the right move and the bottom entry is the up move, as in 2 over 3.
The scalar a . b = |a||b| cos theta, computed component by component; it measures how much of b points along a, and it is zero exactly when the vectors are perpendicular.
The vector of a point measured from the origin: it is pinned to the origin, so moving the point changes its position vector.
A free vector that gives the direction of a line or plane edge: the same arrow drawn anywhere is the same direction vector, as in r = a + lambda b.
Position vectors are pinned to the origin, so every vector feels pinned. Free vectors slide: the same arrow drawn anywhere is the same vector. Only position vectors are pinned to the origin.
